title: INIO IPO lockup ends — Innio N.V., 180 days after its 2026-06-03 prospectus
source: SEC: 424B4 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2109150/000119312526256992/liberty_-_424b4.htm, fetched 2026-10-20 (scripts/research/lockup-discovery.mjs). Prospectus dated 2026-06-03 (read from its cover); 180 days after it is 2026-11-30. Lock-up clause: "Substantially all of our existing shareholders, including the selling shareholder, are subject to lock-up agreements with the underwriters of this offering that restrict the shareholders’ ability to transfer common shares for 180 days from the date of this prospectus, subject to certain exceptions." Re-read in full 2026-10-31 (initial research): the eligible-for-sale table reads "beginning 181 days after the date of this prospectus... all remaining shares will become eligible", so 2026-11-30 is the last locked day and 2026-12-01 the first sellable session; no earnings, price or blackout trigger, only a discretionary waiver by Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley. The Q3 10-Q filed 2026-10-27 repeats the 180-day text from 2026-06-03 with no amendment, and records the over-allotment exercised in full.
notes: $2.43B offering (103.5M shares incl. the full over-allotment, all sold by AI Alpine). The holder keeps 646.5M of 750.0M shares (86.2%); free float is 103.5M. Insiders may first sell on 2026-12-01; unregistered sales are capped by Rule 144 at roughly 31M shares a quarter, so size needs a registered secondary. The pullback the lockup-expiry playbook studies (#5912) is the supply that unlocks then.
